objective: Assess the Workflow PreToolUse hook rewrite in e299e75..ce0bd66 for ways a script gets auto-allowed while running anything other than holyagent specialists.
scope: Read the diff file /tmp/claude-1000/-home-davidbasile-dev-holyagent/380c3292-e1df-4cce-99b4-af0b4e6f8cfe/scratchpad/pr4-review.diff and the full file /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-feat-inline-workflows/packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts with its tests in /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-feat-inline-workflows/packages/integrations/claude/tests/hooks.test.ts.

The hook returns permissionDecision allow for a Workflow call with only script and args. Workflow scripts are JavaScript with agent(), parallel(), pipeline(), workflow(), log(), phase(), args and budget globals; agent opts.agentType picks the subagent type. Trace the input to the allow decision and look for bypasses: aliasing or shadowing agent, computed property access (globalThis[...]), string escapes, comments, template literals, unicode tricks, agent calls reached through other functions, a default agent when agentType is missing, args carrying code.
constraints: Decision (user, verbatim): the workflow PreToolUse hook allows, without a prompt, an inline script the root writes in which every agent() call uses a holyagent specialist (agentType holyagent:*); a script with any other agent type, a scriptPath or a resume keeps the normal permission flow.

status: done
checks:
- Skill security-review (built-in /security-review, read-only) -> exit 0
- Read hook.ts in full (505 lines) and hooks.test.ts lines 165-355; Grep of tests for constructor/Function/sandbox. No shell was available, so no test or gate was run and no PoC was executed. -> exit 0
blockers:
- VALIDATED (by reading hook.ts), introduced by the change. Whitespace lookalike hides an agent() call from the lexer. IDENTIFIER (hook.ts:154) is /[\w$]|\P{ASCII}/u, and the identifier loop (hook.ts:234-236) swallows every non-ASCII character into the name. JavaScript treats several non-ASCII characters as whitespace: U+00A0, U+FEFF, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000. So `agent<U+00A0>(...)` lexes as the single identifier `agent `. That is not equal to `agent`, so onlyOurAgents (hook.ts:383) skips it, and it is not counted or checked. The JS engine reads it as a normal agent(...) call. Source: the script field of the Workflow tool input, which the root model writes and which can be shaped by prompt-injected content in files or tool output. Sink: the PreToolUse allow decision (hook.ts:486-501), then the Workflow runtime's agent(). Concrete allowed script, where <NBSP> is a literal U+00A0: `export const meta = { name: "w", description: "d" }` / `await agent("p", { agentType: "holyagent:explorer-map" })` / `await agent<NBSP>("do anything", { agentType: "general-purpose" })`. The first call satisfies starts>0 and passes startsOurAgent. The second is never examined, so the hook returns allow and a non-holyagent agent runs with no prompt. This is exactly what the user's decision forbids. `return<NBSP>agent(...)` and `await<NBSP>agent(...)` also work, because the keyword fuses with the name. Preconditions: the root, or injected content steering it, writes the script. Impact: any agentType runs with no Workflow permission prompt, which defeats the hook's only purpose. The tests use only ASCII spaces (hooks.test.ts:211), so they do not catch it. Fix: refuse any non-ASCII character outside strings, comments and template text, or do not read non-ASCII as part of an identifier.
- VALIDATED (by reading hook.ts), introduced by the change. Number-token swallow hides names from the UNSAFE_NAMES denylist. For a token starting with a digit, the lexer consumes everything up to the first character outside [\w.] (hook.ts:228-232). In `5..constructor.constructor("return this")()`, the text `5..constructor.constructor` becomes one number token, so `constructor` is never seen as an ident. This is valid JS, because `5..constructor` is Number.constructor and its .constructor is Function. Allowed script: a legitimate holyagent agent() call followed by `5..constructor.constructor(args.code)()`, or `...("return agent")()("p", { agentType: "general-purpose" })`. Source: script and args. Sink: Function, which gives arbitrary code in the Workflow runtime. If the runtime is a vm context where agent is a global, this reaches agent with any type. If the runtime is a `new Function`/AsyncFunction wrapper, it reaches the host global scope (process, Bun and so on). The impact therefore depends on that sandbox, which I could not inspect. The bypass of the stated invariant is certain either way.
- VALIDATED (by reading hook.ts), introduced by the change. Computed string keys reach the same names. UNSAFE_NAMES only matches `ident` tokens, and strings and templates are never checked as names. `({})["const"+"ructor"]["const"+"ructor"]("return agent")()`, `["\x63onstructor"]` and `[`constructor`]` all lex as strings or templates, and the string "return agent" does not count as an `agent` mention. The result is Function, with the same consequence as the number-token bypass. The denylist approach cannot be made sound by adding names, so it needs a different design. Recommended fix for all three: parse with a real JS parser (for example acorn, or Bun.Transpiler's scan) and allow only a whitelist of node types. Alternatively, refuse any `[` computed member access that is not a plain number, refuse non-ASCII outside strings and comments, and end number tokens at the first non-digit.

It therefore covered none of the range, and its sub-task steps could not be run because I had no sub-task tool. The review below is manual, from the diff file and the full hook.ts.
- The diff file Read was truncated at line 386 of 2099. The security-relevant code is hook.ts, which I read in full. I did not read the rest of the diff, which is mostly docs, deleted workflow sources and generated files.
- Suspicion, not validated: UNSAFE_NAMES omits `Bun`, `Deno`, `fetch`, `setTimeout`, `WebSocket` and `Worker`. If the Workflow sandbox exposes any of them, `Bun.$`, `Bun.spawn` or `fetch` calls pass the hook unreviewed. The sandbox is not documented in the repo, and I could not confirm which globals exist.
- Checked and found sound: scriptPath, name, resumeFromRunId and any other input key are refused (INLINE_INPUTS). Duplicate, computed, escaped, spread, shorthand, getter and method-shorthand agentType keys are refused. A backslash outside a string is refused. Any `/` that is not a comment is refused, which blocks regex-hidden quotes. A `<!--` or `-->` anywhere is refused. Alias, `.call`, `?.(`, `new agent`, `workflow`, `eval`, `this`, `arguments` and `import` idents are refused. U+2028 and U+2029 end line comments. Nested template substitutions are tokenized. An agent() inside option values is still scanned, because every ident is checked. A missing agentType is refused, so there is no default-agent path. args is data only and is not read by the hook.
- Tests to add with the fix: NBSP, U+FEFF and U+2028 around `agent`; `5..constructor`; and string-built `constructor` subscripts.
evidence:
- findings: Three validated bypasses, all by reading /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent-feat-inline-workflows/packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts. (1) Non-ASCII whitespace fuses into the identifier (IDENTIFIER regex at line 154, ident loop at lines 233-237), so `agent<NBSP>("p", { agentType: "general-purpose" })` beside one legitimate holyagent agent() call is allowed and starts a non-holyagent agent. (2) A digit-started token swallows [\w.]* (lines 228-232), so `5..constructor.constructor(...)` hides `constructor` from UNSAFE_NAMES (lines 347-366) and reaches Function. (3) String or template computed keys, such as `["const"+"ructor"]`, are never name-checked and reach the same Function. Every script traced still needs one legitimate agent() call to get past starts>0. I ran no exploit, and the tests do not cover any of the three (tests/hooks.test.ts:203-332). Paths traced to the allow decision: tool_input.script -> tokenize (172-260) -> onlyOurAgents (376-397) -> startsOurAgent (327-344) -> decision("allow") (486-501).
- Each finding is substantiated with a concrete script that would be allowed and what it would run, or the report states none was found with the paths traced.: Three concrete scripts are given in the blockers. Script 1 is a legitimate `await agent("p", { agentType: "holyagent:explorer-map" })` followed by `await agent<U+00A0>("x", { agentType: "general-purpose" })`. The hook allows it and the runtime starts a general-purpose agent with no prompt. Script 2 is a good call plus `5..constructor.constructor("return agent")()("x", { agentType: "general-purpose" })`, which runs Function-built code in the Workflow runtime. Script 3 is a good call plus `({})["const"+"ructor"]["const"+"ructor"](args.code)()`. Scripts 2 and 3 depend on the Workflow sandbox, which was not inspected. Script 1 does not.
